output:
Dear all,

I’ve just come off nights and caught up with the thread. First, Amma and Appa, I am genuinely thrilled that you’re coming. Having you here for ordinary days together, not just a hurried holiday, means so much to me. Anika has already made a laminated welcome timetable, including “Paati teaches us rasam, Tuesdays”. Apparently your Tuesdays are spoken for, Amma, though everything else is negotiable.

Kiran, you’re right that I should have spoken to you earlier. I started the visa paperwork because the agent needed my sponsor letter and bank statements, and I should have brought you into the conversation then. Instead, you heard when it sounded as though everything was settled. I’m sorry. That’s on me.

The idea first came up on the phone in August, when Rohan showed Appa the vegetable patch and Appa said, “I could grow drumsticks there.” We’ve talked about it since, and I got excited about making it possible. That explains how we got here; it doesn’t excuse not telling you.

On Appa’s heart, I agree that we need a proper plan. I wouldn’t want any of us relying on “Meera’s a doctor, it’ll be fine”. Dr. Prakash has agreed to review Appa in March before the flight and do a video consultation in July. He’s also happy to share his notes with me, with Appa’s permission, so we can keep the medical information together.

I have a travel insurance quote with pre-existing cardiac cover, at about £640 each for the six months. The agent says Appa’s stent is covered, but this is still a quote, not a policy in place. We need to check the actual wording, exclusions and emergency arrangements before buying it. You’re right that we shouldn’t assume NHS treatment would be free. Leicester Royal is fifteen minutes from our house and I know many of the cardiology team, which is reassuring practically, but it isn’t a substitute for proper insurance or Dr. Prakash’s advice.

The annexe at the back is finished: ground floor, no steps, and its own shower with a grab rail. So there’s space for both of you to have some privacy and your own routine, rather than being in the middle of our household all day.

And Kiran, your point about six weeks is fair. Amma, there’s no obligation to stay six months just because that’s what we’re planning for. The return ticket will be flexible, and if you want to go home earlier, you can. The visa we’re applying for is the UK long-term visitor visa, but that still means a maximum of six months per visit. The proposed dates are the first week of April to the end of September 2027, not a commitment you have to stick out.

Pune and Ganesh Chaturthi needn’t be lost either. One possibility is to fly from here to Pune in September and finish the trip there. Or could the Pune lot come here in August? I’d be very happy to cover your flights. That isn’t a replacement for the festival plans, but it would be lovely to have everyone together.

Could we all have a video call this Sunday at 4pm UK / 9.30pm India? I’d like us to talk through the worries and possibilities properly, and hear what Amma and Appa want too.

Love,
Meera
